content:
I use Lean 4.29 in VS Code on a 15 inch screen. When I have an editor and the info view side by side (horizontally), and the editor accomodates a bit over 80 columns, there remain less than 50 columns for the InfoView.

docs#Lean.MessageData seems to share relevant features of docs#Std.Format. I guess it should be possible to MessageData → String with different widths. But what in fact seems to happen, is that logInfo and others always render to a fixed width in the InfoView. The fixed width seems to be exactly the default of docs#Std.Format.pretty (docs#Std.Format.defWidth = 120). That can be witnessed by observing and comparing the outputs of the following logInfos in a narrow info view:

import Lean
open Lean

def s : String      := "0123456789"
def l : List String := List.replicate 50 s
def f : Format      := repr l

run_meta logInfo f
run_meta logInfo f.pretty
run_meta logInfo (f.pretty (width := 40) (indent := 2))

In a narrow InfoView, the outputs of logInfo f and logInfo f.pretty (using the default width of 120) look the same and contain lines broken by the UI, not by a MessageData → String with a width that fits the InfoView.

Is there a way to set the width for the info view? Why does it not happen automatically/adaptively? Is it intentional for some reason or a missing feature?
This topic was moved here from #Editors & UIs > Width and intentation of MessageData in info view (VS Code) by Sebastian Miele.

Everyone runs into this eventually, it seems... :upside_down: I'm going to make an RFC, unless I can find more pre-existing discussion. I'll also link this to #lean4 > pretty print format with no whitespace.
I've now made a Zulip RFC about this: #lean4 > RFC: pretty-printing with infinite width Hopefully it will become a real RFC soon.
